# Satipaṭṭhānakathā (Ps 3.8)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Satipaṭṭhānakathā* ("Discussion of Mindfulness Meditation") is the eighth treatise of the third vagga (or division) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 3.8), corresponding to PTS volume II, pages 232–235 [Anālayo 2006]. Alongside the treatise of the same name in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 155–159) and the Abhidhamma's *Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga* (Vibh 193–207), it represents an analytical scholastic treatment of the four establishments of mindfulness within the Theravāda canonical literature [Anālayo 2006; Anālayo 2010].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates significant internal text reuse across the Pāli canon, sharing substantial passages with other treatises of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* itself—predominantly the *Ānāpānassatikathā* (Ps 1.3) and *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits direct textual links with early discourse expositions on mindfulness, notably the *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47), the *Anuruddha Saṁyutta* (SN 52), and the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Suttas* of the Dīgha and Majjhima Nikāyas (DN 22 and MN 10), as well as the Abhidhamma's *Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 7) [DharmaNexus]. Passages from the text are heavily cited and mirrored in later exegetical works, including the *Visuddhimagga* and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus show thematic and formulaic parallels in Chinese collections such as the *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) and *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99), as well as Tibetan Mahāyāna works including the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* and the *Akṣayamatinirdeśasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
